title: "Anticipant"-TIPS After a First Portal-hypertension-related Complication in Cirrhosis
official: "Anticipant"-TIPS After a First Portal-hypertension-related Complication in Cirrhosis: a Multicenter, Superiority, Randomized, Controlled Trial, in Parallel Groups
summary: Further decompensation (FD) in cirrhosis represents a prognostic stage associated with an even higher mortality than that associated with the first decompensation. The Baveno VII conference defined FD as a second portal hypertension (PH)-driven decompensating event (ascites, VB, or hepatic encephalopathy) and/or jaundice, or development of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis and/or hepatorenal syndrome-acute kidney injury HRS-AKI. This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effect of TIPS versus standard of care on survival without further decompensation during a 24-month follow up period in patients with cirrhosis after a first PH-related decompensation.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Women and men,
* 18 years \< age ≤ 65 years,
* With cirrhosis and a first PH-related complication defined as a first episode of variceal bleeding and/or a first episode of ascites requiring a paracentesis of \> 2 liters (max 2 paracenteses),
* Affiliated to a social insurance system,
* Having signed the written informed consent to participate in the study
* The diagnosis of cirrhosis will be based on Baveno VI conference

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patients with variceal bleeding and an indication of TIPS (salvage or pre-emptive TIPS)
* Patients with recurrent ascites (\> 2 LVP)
* Common contraindication for TIPS (MELD (Model for End stage Liver Disease) score \> 18, Child Pugh score \>11 (Appendix 7), Previous overt recurrent/chronic hepatic encephalopathy except during the index episode and High risk of post TIPS cardiac failure.)
* Hepatocellular carcinoma
* Previous liver transplantation
* Previous derivation procedure
* Untreated chronic viral B or C hepatitis
* Uncontrolled systemic infection/sepsis
* Pregnant or breastfeeding women
* Inability to receive an enlightened information
* Patients participating to another research program
* Patients placed under judicial protection
* No ability for the participant to comply with the requirement of the study
